scope: Purposive complete overall podium sample for ShellHacks 2019, 2020 and 2021: 9 projects, not all sponsor winners.
method: Award labels verified in each project's event-specific Submitted to block on Devpost, not inferred from gallery position. Technical and outcome claims are participant descriptions, not independently reproduced. Features use yes or unknown; unknown means not documented clearly, not absent. A documented interface can be an incomplete prototype. External service includes hosting/database; open-source libraries alone do not qualify. Hardware evidence is described explicitly so commodity camera use can be separated from custom electronics.

editions.overall_criteria: No substantive rubric published in the overview. Generic Judging Criteria says to submit the project; overall award descriptions do not explain scoring.
editions.dates_note: Event description gives September 20–22, 2019; Devpost date header gives September 21–22.
editions.coverage_note: All three overall places verified. Gallery page one shows 18 winner-labelled projects; a complete award census was not performed. Devpost participant count is not event attendance.

editions.overall_criteria: Creativity, execution and impact; all submissions automatically entered for overall categories.
editions.coverage_note: All three overall places verified. Full unique award count not established; the gallery intermittently returned a JavaScript verification page, but indexed results and each podium project page were readable. Wolfram Award is broad recognition for the Top 30 and explicitly requires neither Wolfram use nor specific criteria. Do not treat it as evidence of Wolfram integration.

editions.overall_criteria: Creativity, execution and impact; all submissions automatically entered for overall categories. The generic Judging Criteria section directs users to individual challenge descriptions.
editions.coverage_note: All three overall places verified. Gallery page one shows 21 winner-labelled projects before nonwinners; full census not performed. Participant count is platform registration, not attendance.

projects.name: Freetear
projects.award_verification: Devpost Submitted to ShellHacks 2019: Winner First Place Overall.
projects.problem: Developers lose time configuring deployment, databases and hosting for side projects.
projects.workflow: CLI templates an application and automates connections to free-tier deployment services.
projects.feature_evidence: Describes free-tier service credential automation, an NPM CLI and React/HTML UI work. No explicit AI, inclusion, social-good or hardware component documented.
projects.prototype_evidence: Team reports implementing service login/creation scripts and templates; GitHub and deployment links supplied.
projects.limits: No measured deployment-time improvement or independent validation.

projects.name: No Vote Left Behind
awards_exact: JP Morgan Chase & Co. - Best Hack for Social Good
projects.award_verification: All three labels appear under Submitted to ShellHacks 2019.
projects.problem: People with limited time or resources face voter-registration barriers.
projects.workflow: Raspberry Pi generates QR/RFID credentials; a web form fills an official registration PDF and sends it to the relevant jurisdiction.
projects.feature_evidence: Explicit underserved-voter goal, Raspberry Pi circuit and web form; Azure and fax integration described. Machine learning appears only in future plans and is not counted as implemented.
projects.prototype_evidence: Team describes a working example and implementation responsibilities.
projects.limits: No independent election-process, security or real registration validation; do not adopt team's security claims as verified.

projects.name: sock.it
projects.award_verification: Both labels appear under Submitted to ShellHacks 2019.
projects.problem: Caregivers need information about an infant's heart rate, oxygen levels and sleep.
projects.workflow: Senses heart rate and oxygen saturation; the public description stops before explaining the subsequent data flow.
projects.feature_evidence: Infant-health objective and sensing explicitly stated; Arduino and Pusher listed. React tag alone does not establish a documented interface.
projects.prototype_evidence: GitHub link supplied; hardware award verified.
projects.limits: Most narrative sections empty. No clinical accuracy, completed UI or alerting workflow established.

projects.name: Farsense
projects.award_verification: Both labels appear under Submitted to ShellHacks 2020.
projects.problem: Remote environmental monitoring can help assess disaster-related property and environmental damage.
projects.workflow: Battery-powered sensor stations send weather observations over a LoRa mesh to a dashboard.
projects.feature_evidence: Explicit environmental/disaster goal, dashboard and sensor components. Open-source LoRa library described; no external hosted service or ML implementation established.
projects.prototype_evidence: Team reports two working sensor stations and supplies photographs/video and GitHub.
projects.limits: Damage prediction is a potential use; an operational predictive model or disaster-outcome improvement is not established.

projects.name: Social Distance Beer Pong
projects.award_verification: Both labels appear under Submitted to ShellHacks 2020.
projects.problem: Friends wanted to play a familiar social game while remaining physically distant during COVID-19.
projects.workflow: Infrared cup sensors and a microcontroller send data by USB to a C++ terminal game.
projects.feature_evidence: Explicit pandemic-distancing purpose; physical sensors and terminal interface. Social benefit here is participant-stated safe social connection, not measured health impact.
projects.prototype_evidence: Team reports a completed physical prototype and links video and GitHub.
projects.limits: No remote network architecture or measured disease-risk reduction documented; terminal interface counts as interaction, not polished graphical UI.

projects.name: CloudPlate
awards_exact: Best Potential Startup by 1517 Fund (Undergraduate students only)
projects.award_verification: Three labels appear under Submitted to ShellHacks 2020. AutoNation award NOT listed despite matching its challenge.
projects.problem: Dealership arrival and service check-in can be slow and impersonal.
projects.workflow: Camera/OCR identifies an arriving car; dashboard displays customer and service records; personalized SMS greets the customer.
projects.feature_evidence: Cloud OCR/ML, API orchestration and dashboard screenshots documented; hardware is commodity cameras reportedly costing $15, not custom electronics.
projects.prototype_evidence: Page shows demonstration GIFs and claims low-light camera operation.
projects.limits: No quantified time savings or accuracy benchmark; repository kept private, code submitted as archive.

projects.name: Tango
projects.award_verification: Label appears specifically under ShellHacks 2021; another event submission is also listed.
projects.problem: At-home dance learners lack interactive feedback from one-way tutorials.
projects.workflow: Pose estimation compares a learner to a reference routine; timing and body-size adjustments support live annotations, charts and replay.
projects.feature_evidence: AI pose library and feedback charts explicitly described. ngrok is listed, so external service is yes under a broad hosting/tunnelling definition; MediaPipe itself is a library, not evidence of a cloud AI API.
projects.prototype_evidence: Video, code and team account of working annotation/data-visualization components.
projects.limits: No validated coaching efficacy; responsive layout and robust edge-case handling are future work. Ordinary video input is not counted as custom hardware.

projects.name: Bizchain
awards_exact: Best Use of Notifications by Courier
CryptoCurrency Portfolio/Trading Application by CoinRoutes Inc.
projects.award_verification: All three labels appear under Submitted to ShellHacks 2021.
projects.problem: Consumers and local merchants face complex cryptocurrency payments and portfolio management.
projects.workflow: Shop at local merchants, manage crypto holdings, run trading strategies and receive price alerts.
projects.feature_evidence: Regression price model, external market/notification APIs and dashboard illustrated. Stated support for local businesses establishes a community-economic objective, not demonstrated benefit.
projects.prototype_evidence: Detailed API architecture, custom dataset, Figma prototype, demonstration images and GitHub.
projects.limits: No investment-return or model-accuracy validation; shopping/portfolio integration remained an improvement area. Financial simplicity is not coded as disability accessibility.

projects.name: Kudos
awards_exact: Best Use of Google Cloud by Google
projects.award_verification: Both labels appear under the event link resolving to shellhacks2021.devpost.com, labelled ShellHacks on this project page.
projects.problem: Students and other users struggled to maintain productivity during the pandemic.
projects.workflow: Collaborate on tasks/projects and earn completion rewards; public page primarily documents design and intended app behavior.
projects.feature_evidence: Firebase backend, Figma interaction flows and design implementation documented.
projects.prototype_evidence: GitHub and Figma prototype linked; team reports completed design implementation.
projects.limits: Explicit future work includes fixing authentication, continuing mobile-app construction and implementing reward finances. This is a counterexample to claims that all winners had a complete working product.

cross_case_cautions: The sample establishes recurring documented properties among winners; without comparable nonwinners it cannot estimate causal winning factors or probabilities.
Do not equate a public demo/code link with a tested live deployment or independently validated outcomes.
Sponsor wins are exact labels, not inferred from sponsor technologies; CloudPlate matched AutoNation's challenge but did not list that award.
Commonality is not universality: hardware, AI, social purpose and fully implemented workflows differ markedly across these nine winners.
Tango and Bizchain have richer pages than sock.it; counting undocumented properties as absent would introduce documentation bias.
Generic social impact and accessibility must remain separate. Productivity, easy UX and low price alone do not establish inclusion-focused design.
Public project pages can change after the event, so descriptions may not be a frozen record of the judging-time implementation.
